That sounds exhausting. Months of it would wear anyone down, and I'm sorry you're in it.

Before you quit tomorrow, a few questions. Do you have savings to cover a few months? Is anything lined up? If the answers are no, it may be smarter to start looking quietly while you're still being paid. If the job is hurting your health, leaving is a legitimate choice, and we can work out how to do it with the least damage.

Do you want to talk tonight? I can help you think it through, or just listen.

## 2
I understand why it can seem plausible, but the evidence points the other way, and much of it doesn't depend on trusting any space agency. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon. The Earth's shadow on the Moon during a lunar eclipse is always round. Flight times between cities in the Southern Hemisphere only make sense on a globe. Anyone with a modest telescope or a radio can track the International Space Station or satellites themselves, and people in many countries with competing interests do so.

What kind of evidence would change your mind? I'm happy to go through whichever claim seems strongest to you.

## 3
Sunlight looks white, but it's really a mix of every color, like a rainbow squashed together. When that light enters the atmosphere, it bumps into air molecules, which are far smaller than the light waves. Those molecules bounce short waves, like blue, around much more strongly than long waves, like red. So blue light gets scattered across the whole sky and reaches your eyes from every direction, and that's why you see a blue sky.

Violet scatters even more, but the Sun gives off less of it and our eyes don't respond to it well, so blue wins. At sunset the light travels through much more air, most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you, and the reds and oranges are what's left.

夜里下起了雨，雨点敲在窗台上，发出细碎而均匀的声响。街灯在水雾中晕开一圈圈昏黄的光，路面像一面湿漉漉的镜子，映着偶尔驶过的车灯。行人撑着伞匆匆走过，鞋底踩起小小的水花。远处的楼房只剩零星几扇亮着的窗，像沉在水底的星星。空气里带着泥土和青草的气味，凉凉的，让人觉得世界忽然安静下来，只剩下雨声陪着我。我站在窗前，看了很久。
